title.narrative: Strategic Integration in Sustainable Polder Development: Transformative Model for Resilient Livelihoods and In-Polder Water Management

description.narrative: The "Polders of the Future" Action Research Programme (ARP) aims to foster sustainable in-polder water management and resilient livelihoods in Polder 31, located in the southwest coastal region of Bangladesh. Anchored in participatory, community-driven processes, the ARP addresses long-standing institutional and operational challenges, including the recurrent Build-Neglect-Rebuild (BNR) cycle in polder development.Partners for Water financing covers the initial six month inception phase (in 2025) by the Center for Environmental and Geographic Information Services (CEGIS), the Institute of Water Modelling (IWM), and Uttaran. The ARP is structured into two strategic pathways:1. Piloting socio-technical water management solutions and low-hanging livelihood interventions; and2. Co-learning and advocacy to inform institutional reform and policy innovation.Through stakeholder consultations, institutional design, and demonstration pilots, the ARP will develop an implementation plan for Integrated Polder Water Management (IPWM) plans and strengthen Water Management Organizations (WMOs). It will also facilitate coordination among the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB), local government institutions (LGIs), non-governmental organisations (NGOs), and local communities.The programme emphasises a three-tier co-learning model – linking local, technical, and policy actors – to ensure systemic change, build capacity, and promote upscaling. Insights will feed into improving national policies such as the Guidelines for Participatory Water Management (GPWM) and DPP, and inform the development of a replicable and scalable model for resilient polder governance.
